page: Microsoft Azure D2alds_v6 is an entry-level general purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core running 2 threads at 3.7 GHz. System hardware includes 4.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), 32 MB of L3 cache, and a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 support), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. It operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluation highlights robust single-core processing capabilities, placing in the top 25% for both stress-ng single-core performance (3078.68) and Geekbench single-core score (2078.0). Single-threaded decompression with bzip3 (13.49 GB/sec) and gzip compression (29.24 GB/sec) reach average tier throughput. Conversely, total multi-threaded compute remains constrained by the 2-vCPU ceiling, reflected in bottom-quartile metrics across Geekbench multi-core (2615.0), PassMark CPU score (3829.46), and Clang software compilation (2807.0).

Memory subsystem testing reveals low overall capacity and throughput, with PassMark memory scoring in the bottom 25% (1333.2) and cached read bandwidth ranking in the lowest 10% (151.2 GB/sec). Large-block write performance maintains average levels at 27.75 GB/sec, while read-only large blocks yield 37.16 GB/sec. Application testing displays moderate output for low-footprint workloads, such as LLM text generation on a 135M parameter model at 100.32 tokens/sec, but struggles under heavy concurrent operations, recording 2.96 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.44 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

Azure D2alds_v6 offers high per-thread execution efficiency within a cost-conscious, low-memory footprint. The integrated 118 GB NVMe SSD provides localized scratch space, though memory-intensive database engines and parallel batch processing are restricted by the 4.0 GB RAM pool. The instance is suitable for single-threaded microservices, lightweight web utilities, low-scale container hosts, and background automation tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure D2alds_v6 is a general purpose instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 1 physical core powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor at 3.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Hyper-V virtualization, it includes 4.0 GB of memory and a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD. The CPU supports modern vector and cryptographic instruction sets, including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core CPU throughput in the upper 25%, balanced against entry-level multi-core and memory subsystem capacity due to its dual-thread configuration. With no GPU hardware, it represents an efficient low-resource profile for single-threaded utilities, microservices, light web hosting, and auxiliary tasks requiring high per-core execution speeds coupled with fast temporary local NVMe storage.
